model.name: Model for omeprazole absorption in the intestine

notes.body:
Model for omeprazole absorption in the intestine and the stomach pH
Application forms
The oral dose is in the stomach (PODOSE_<sid>, mg). The form is set by the switches f_ec and f_unprotected:
buffered solution or suspension (f_ec = 0, f_unprotected = 0): the dose enters the intestinal lumen with Ka_dis_ome, no degradation.
unprotected solution or suspension (f_ec = 0, f_unprotected = 1): the fraction F_ome_pH (depending on the stomach pH) enters the lumen, the rest is degraded by the gastric acid.
enteric-coated form (f_ec = 1): the pellets leave the stomach with Ka_ec_ome (POEC_<sid>, mg, pellets in the small intestine) and release omeprazole with the same rate into the lumen: a delayed release (two steps), no degradation.
food (fed = 1): the gastric emptying and the dissolution are slower by FED_f_dissolution, the fraction absorbed is FED_f_absorption.
Absorption
S- and R-omeprazole are absorbed with OMEABS_k, completely (F_ome_abs = 1, no unchanged omeprazole in the feces); the bioavailability is the hepatic first pass.
Proton pumps and stomach pH
The model describes the change in stomach pH depending on omeprazole. A key component are the proton pumps in the parietal cells.
proton-pumps (PP) in gastric wall (gastric parietal cells, protein amount)
PP can be inhibited by omeprazole in the gastric wall; the activation processes from omeprazole to the active inhibitor in the gastric wall are not modeled in detail, but omeprazole was assumed to directly inhibit the PPs.
inhibition of PP converts the active in the inactive form
PP have a continuous turnover consisting of PP protein synthesis and PP degradation. The newly synthesized PP protein is active. Active and inactive PP are degraded identically.
pH in the stomach is modeled by calculating the amount of protons in the stomach.
PP (active) can secrete protons in the lumen (-> decrease pH)
only omeprazole, but not the omeprazole metabolites were assumed to have proton pump inhibitor (PPI) activity.
PP (active) + OME -> PP-OME (inactive) --synthesis--> PP (active) PP (active) --degradation--> PP-OME (inactive) --degradation-->
pH calculation
pH is calculated as decimal logarithm of reciprocal hydrogen ion activity pH = - log10 ([H+]). [H+] is in [mole/litre] = [mmole/litre] in stomach volume.
The normal stomach pH values are: pH=1-3
gastric acid secretion
A typical adult human stomach will secrete about 1.5 liters of gastric acid daily.
Stomach volume is around 100 [ml]
PP pump H+ into [gastric acid]; [gastric acid] --1.5 [l/day]--> [stomach (100[ml])] --1.5 [l/day]-->.
1.5 [l/day] = 1.5 [l/day]/(24*60 [min/day])* 1000 [ml/l] = 1.04 [ml/min]
acid output basal: 4.3 [mmole (H+)/hr] placebo => 4.3 mmole/100 ml = 0.043 mmole/ml = 43 mole/litre (in 1 hr). Delta pH (1 hr) = - log10(43) = -1.63
stimulated (food stimulated): ~ 8 [mmole (H+)/hr] = 70-80 [mole/litre]. Delta pH (1 hr) = - log10(350) = -1.88
stimulated (pentagastrin): 35 [mmole (H+)/hr] = 350 [mole/litre]. Delta pH (1 hr) = - log10(350) = -2.54
pH changes
Stomach pH should be ~1-3 pH at steady state and go up to ~7 pH at maximum PP inhibition at 80-90%.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

parameter.name: enteric-coated form (0 solution or suspension, 1 enteric-coated)

body.p: 1: capsule with enteric-coated pellets, enteric-coated tablet, MUPS tablet, enteric-coated granules; 0: solution or suspension. Set by the experiments from the application form.

parameter.name: unprotected solution (0 buffered or enteric-coated, 1 unprotected)

body.p: 1: a solution or suspension without bicarbonate buffer, which the gastric acid degrades (F_ome_pH); 0: buffered solution or suspension and the enteric-coated forms. Set by the experiments.

parameter.name: rate of the gastric emptying of a solution

body.p: Gastric emptying of a buffered solution: tmax 0.2-0.3 hr [Andersson1990a, Andersson1993, Naesdal1986, Regaardh1990]. Fast, not fitted: the absorption OMEABS_k limits the uptake, the fits spread the rate over 9-60 /hr at the same cost.

parameter.name: rate of the gastric emptying and the release of an enteric-coated form

body.p: The enteric-coated pellets leave the stomach and dissolve in the small intestine, both with this rate (a delayed release): tmax 1.5-2.5 hr [Elkoshi2002, Palovaara2003, Uno2007].
The value of GU__Ka_ec_ome is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: fed effect on the gastric emptying and dissolution

body.p: A meal slows the gastric emptying of the enteric-coated pellets: tmax +1.5 to +3 hr, Cmax x0.34-0.40 (VazdaSilva2005, high-fat breakfast). Not fitted (one study).

parameter.name: fed effect on the fraction absorbed

body.p: A meal lowers the exposure: AUC x0.62-0.66 at steady state (VazdaSilva2005, high-fat breakfast). Not fitted (one study).
Omeprazole is absorbed completely: the urinary recovery of the radioactivity is the same after IV and oral doses, no unchanged omeprazole in the feces [Regaardh1986, Andersson1993]. Not fitted.
The value of GU__OMEABS_k is the result of the fit PK_20261020_090631__aa2cf, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate of the fecal excretion of the other metabolites

body.p: Transit of the metabolites of the bile from the intestinal lumen into the feces, half-life about 16 hr. Not fitted.
